mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% triggers a preemptive equity risk premium, as investors anticipate future rate hikes, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during confirmed inflation spikes, or CPIAUCSL remains below 0.3% for ≥3 consecutive months without subsequent positive returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS labor compensation growth signals wage stickiness and upward wage pressure, which elevates expected corporate profits and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS month-over-month growth rate > 0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant positive 60-day forward returns during confirmed wage growth acceleration (Granger causality rejected, or IC < -0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in HOUST retail sales above the prior quarter's average, accompanied by a decline in RSAFS inventory drawdowns, indicates strengthening consumer demand, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > Q1 prior quarter median AND RSAFS < Q1 prior quarter median in the current month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite meeting trigger condition in ≥60% of similar events (Granger causality F-stat < 1.0).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in INDPRO manufacturing index coinciding with a sharp rise in GDPC1 personal consumption expenditure suggests supply-side constraints, which elevates risk premia and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO month-over-month decline > 5% AND GDPC1 month-over-month growth > 2% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain non-negative during confirmed supply shocks (IC > 0.15 over 60-day window).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent 3-month decline in FEDFUNDS rates without a subsequent rise predicts a flattening of real discount rates, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days in a steady-state regime.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during 3 consecutive months of FEDFUNDS declines, or FEDFUNDS recovers before 60 days and returns remain flat.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-time drop in UNRATE unemployment followed by a sustained rise above 4% signals a transition to a labor market tightening, which precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% for one month then rises above 4% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain non-negative during confirmed labor market tightening episodes (IC < -0.1 over 100-day window).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly doubling of PAYEMS employment figures accompanied by a sustained monthly decline in RSAFS retail inventories indicates robust labor market absorption, which elevates equity risk appetite and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 2× prior month AND RSAFS < prior month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive during ≥40% of similar events (IC > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in INDPRO accompanied by a sharp rise in HOUST retail sales (>10% YoY) suggests sector-specific demand shifts without broad supply constraints, which can produce mixed or negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days in a mixed economy regime.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < INDPRO previous year median AND HOUST > HOUST previous year median in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are consistently positive during such events (Granger causality rejected, IC > 0.2).
